title: Residency Proof Automation Playbook and Evidence Aggregator
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Build a playbook and implementation plan for automating generation of residency and retention evidence for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 audits. Deliver a proof bundle format, a lightweight evidence collector spec, and a retention lifecycle enforcement policy so auditors can retrieve auditable artifacts by control mapping, timestamp, and region. Focus on: mapping our telemetry and config to control statements, automating time-windowed evidence harvesting, signed bundle export, and an API for on-demand auditor queries.
background: Customers in regulated industries repeatedly ask for documented, time-bounded evidence that data was stored, processed, and deleted according to residency and retention policies. Current audits are manual, ad-hoc, and costly to compile. This ticket defines a repeatable playbook and minimal implementation for a self-service evidence aggregator tied to our control matrix for SOC 2 and ISO 27001.
acceptance_criteria: Control-to-artifact mapping document covering at least 12 SOC2/ISO controls (storage, backups, logs, access reviews, key management, deletion)
Evidence bundle JSON schema with signed manifests and provenance metadata agreed by security and legal
Collector spec and two reference collectors (config-change events, residency-tagged object list) implemented as engineering spikes
Retention enforcement policy that can generate a 'proof-of-deletion' artifact for records deleted per policy
API contract for auditor queries: /evidence/query and /evidence/bundle/{id} with time-range and region filters
End-to-end demo: generate a bundle for a sample tenant showing data residency in EU region with retention TTL and deletion proof
tasks: Draft control mapping table: map Redwood telemetry and artifacts to SOC2/ISO control items
Work with Security to define bundle signature and integrity model
Define minimal evidence bundle schema and sample manifest
Spec retention lifecycle labels and retention TTL enforcement flows
Design API surface for auditor queries and signed bundle retrieval
Create two collector prototypes (object residency export, retention-event snapshot)
Run demo generation for internal audit team and capture feedback
Document playbook steps for customer-facing runbook and PS engagements
risks: Regulatory variance: regional auditors expect different artifact formats
Privacy: exposing too much metadata could leak customer-sensitive information
Operational cost: collecting high-frequency evidence across many tenants increases storage and processing costs
Legal hold: deletion proofs must respect legal hold scenarios; false deletions could cause compliance incidents
outcomes: Reduced manual audit time by providing pre-packaged, signed evidence bundles
Faster sales cycles for regulated customers with clear residency proof
Baseline spec that can be extended to additional controls and evidence sources
Re-usable collectors that feed Redwood Console evidence explorer
notes: Prefer signed manifests with RFC-compliant timestamps (RFC 3339) and digest hashes for integrity
Evidence bundles should include a minimal redactable layer so customer-identifiable data is not exposed to auditors by default
Consider integrating with KMS to include key-change logs as evidence for key-management controls
Retention enforcement must integrate with object-store lifecycle events and our DB archival worker
